subject: Staging scope exception for private/VPC pilot - product & resourcing asks
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Staging scope exception for private/VPC pilot - product & resourcing asks

Team,

Quick summary: Hearthwell (pilot customer) has asked for the staging environment for their private/VPC deployment to mirror their prod networking (VLAN segmentation + dedicated NAT) and an SFTP jump host we hadn’t scoped. This is a non-standard request for the pilot and would require additional infra work, a short exception to our minimal-staging policy, and a small product change to enable configurable network profiles for the control plane.

Asking:
- Product: can we prioritize a small config surface to pick a "staging profile" (minimal | mirror-prod) so we can ship the pilot without a full feature rollout? Target: a toggle + validation.
- Infra/Infra-Eng (Karthik): estimate effort for building the mirror-prod staging (networking + NAT + SFTP hop). Do we need one-off networking support from Cloud Ops?
- Security (Kimberly/Soojin): are there gating checks (KMS/HSM, logging) that would block doing a quasi-prod staging in a customer VPC?

Attachments: diff doc for staging expectations, capacity estimate workbook, customer MRD with their ask highlighted. Drive folder link in related links.

Timeline: Hearthwell wants a staged demo week of Oct 19 - 23. If we can't provide mirror-prod on staging, they will request an elevated acceptance window which pushes the commercial milestone.

Immediate next steps: Karthik & Kimberly, can you reply with high-level red/amber/green on feasibility + a rough T-shirt estimate by EOD tomorrow? I want to surface any procurement/cloud marketplace implications to Samira before the weekend.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0118

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Staging scope exception for private/VPC pilot - product & resourcing asks

Ben—

Thanks for the heads up. High level: technically doable but we need to validate three items before we sign off:
1) Key management: if the customer wants customer-managed keys in their staging VPC we need a KMS onboarding checklist completed and an HSM exception if they insist on hardware HSM (this takes longer).
2) Audit/logging: staging must still ship audit/export logs to our control plane for monitoring. If the NAT/segmentation blocks egress we need a secure relay pattern.
3) Network posture: the SFTP jump host adds an inbound/exposed element; we need a reviewed runbook and a short threat model.

Can we get Karthik to confirm if the staging VPC will live in our account with peering, or in the customer's AWS account (the latter adds IAM/procurement steps)? If it's in their account we should expect 3-4 business days of networking coordination with their cloud team.

I can draft the KMS/onboarding checklist, but need a product-specified config surface (what fields/toggles) to reference.

-Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Security Lead, Redwood Inference
[kimberly_park@redwood.ai]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Staging scope exception for private/VPC pilot - product & resourcing asks

Folks—

Quick feasibility read: AMBER (doable with clear constraints). Details below.

Scope notes:
- Location: if the staging VPC is provisioned in Hearthwell's AWS account we need their network team to create a dedicated subnet and NAT gateway per our required egress rules. If we host in our account (preferred for speed) we will create a separate VPC with peering and BHW routing; that is ~2-3 engineer days to provision and validate (network infra + VPN/peering).
- SFTP jump host: simple EC2 + security group + NAT; ~6-8 engineer hours to stand up and runbook.
- Mirror-prod network profile: we can add a small config document to control plane (profile name + required fields: cidr, nat-required boolean, sftp-host boolean, egress-relay endpoint). Implementation: ~3-4 dev days (API + UI toggle + validation schema) + 1 day test/QA.
- Oncall & runbook: need a runbook and a short oncall escalation route for the pilot — estimate 1 SRE day to author and 0.2 FTE per week during pilot (rotational).
- Compliance: if customer requires customer-managed KMS with symmetric CMKs in their account, expect 5 business days for onboarding and IAM policy work. If they accept keys in our KMS with CMK import, ~2 days.

Blocking items (if not cleared, project slips):
1) Customer choice of account ownership for staging VPC (their account = longer).
2) KMS/HSM requirement (HSM pushes >3 weeks).
3) Procurement for extra NAT and cross-account networking (if vendor approvals are required).

Requesting resource commitment: 1 infra engineer (2.5 days), 1 backend engineer (4 days), 0.5 SRE (for runbook + oncall rotation), and product/product-design time to add the config surface (2-3 days). If we agree to this headcount, we can hit the Oct 19 demo date with some contingency.

I'll add these estimates to SUP-4123 and upload a short runbook draft to the Drive folder.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Staff Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks all — good summary and appreciated level-setting. Quick updates:

- Samira (cc'd): Hearthwell is OK with the staging VPC living in Redwood's account with peering for the demo week (this removes several procurement delays). They still want a mirror of their prod segmentation but not an HSM.
- Kimberly: KMS will be managed by Redwood for staging (customer confirmed HSM not required), but we do need the audit relay pattern. Please share the checklist when ready.
- Karthik: please open SUP-4123 with your estimates and the runbook draft — I’ll flag the priority to Product to secure the 3-4 dev days you requested.

Next steps/owners:
- Karthik: infra provisioning + runbook draft (owner; due Oct 12)
- Kimberly: KMS/onboarding checklist and threat model review (owner; due Oct 12)
- Soojin/Product: define the minimal config surface (profile toggle + fields) and PRD stub so devs can pick it up (owner; due Oct 9)
- Ben/Sales: update customer acceptance milestone & commercial note if we end up needing >1 week slip.

I'll update HubSpot record and attach the runbook draft once SUP-4123 has the first comment.

Ben
